title: ACA s. 19 — Determination of rules of procedure

content.overview: Section 19 permits the arbitral tribunal, subject to the Act, to conduct proceedings in the manner it considers appropriate and provides that the Code of Civil Procedure and Indian Evidence Act are not binding on the tribunal.
content.glance: Section 19 permits the arbitral tribunal, subject to the Act, to conduct proceedings in the manner it considers appropriate and provides that the Code of Civil Procedure and Indian Evidence Act are not binding on the tribunal.
content.study:
Module 1: Procedural autonomy
The tribunal is not bound by the CPC or Indian Evidence Act, subject to the Act and the parties' agreement.

Module 2: Party agreement
The parties may agree on procedure; where they do not, the tribunal determines procedure within statutory limits.

Module 3: Fairness constraint
Procedural autonomy is bounded by equal treatment and full opportunity under section 18 and by the mandatory provisions of the Act.

examples.title: Rule applies
examples.body: Parties agree a procedural timetable and evidentiary method; the tribunal can apply that agreement subject to mandatory law.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: A tribunal treats procedural autonomy as permission to disregard section 18 or another mandatory statutory safeguard.

hypotheticals.question: Does non-application of CPC mean no procedural discipline?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The tribunal is not bound by CPC, but remains bound by the Act, party agreement and fundamental procedural fairness.

rows.right: CPC is not binding on the tribunal.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 19 as self-contained without reading its statutory conditions.
misconceptions.correction: Apply section 19 with the Act's express conditions and connected provisions.
